test_title: PYST 11: SSC CGL 2022 - English (Held On: 03 Dec 2022 Shift 2)
subject: english
question:
**Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.**

Not only is my brother intelligent __though hard working__ too.
solution:
The correct answer is: **but hard working**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Replace the conjunction "**though**" with "**but**" to correct the sentence.
 
• “**But**” indicates a complete negation and is usually used after a comma, in the middle of a sentence.
 
 
• **For example- ***The food wasn't good, but at least it was cheap.*
 
 
 
• “**Though**” is usually used at the end of a sentence and indicates a partial negation.
 
 
• **For example- ***She seemed healthy, though she is thin.*
 
 
 
• **​**We use "**though**" to introduce a subordinate clause in which you mention something that contrasts with what you are saying in the main clause.
 
• "**But**" is used to add emphasis to a sentence.
 
• The implied meaning of the given sentence is: My sibling is not only smart but also diligent.
 
• Some two-part subjects are joined by “either...or,” “neither...nor,” or “not only...but also.” In these cases, the verb should agree with the subject closest to the verb.
 
• In this sentence, "**not only**" is already mentioned. So, we should use "**but**" according to the subject-verb agreement rule.

Therefore, the correct answer is **option 2** which can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

**Corrected sentence:** *Not only is my brother intelligent but __hard working too.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• Let us look at the use of the other words given in the options.
 
 
• **Or**: Or is a conjunction that connects two or more possibilities or alternatives. It connects words, phrases and clauses which are the same grammatical type.

 
 
• **For example-** *Which do you prefer? Leather or suede?*
 
 
 
• **So**: It is used as a subordinating conjunction to introduce clauses of result or decision.
 
 
• For example- *You are right, of course, so I think we will accept what the bank offers.*
 
 
 
• **Yet**: It is used as an adverb to refer to a time which starts in the past and continues up to the present. We use it mostly in negative statements or questions in the present perfect.
 
 
• For example- *Kevin hasn't registered for class yet.*
